description: A practical packing list for adventure travel in India: the layering system for mountain trips, footwear, and checklists for treks, snow trips, rafting and water sports, desert trips and high-altitude road trips, with a first-aid kit, documents and what you can rent instead of buying.
dek: The right kit is mostly about layers, feet and a few activity-specific items. Here is what to pack for each kind of adventure in India.

about.name: Adventure travel packing list for India

intro: Packing for adventure in India means preparing for very different conditions: humid heat on the coast, cold nights above 4,000 metres, monsoon rain and desert sun. The core of every list is the same, though: layers you can add and remove, footwear suited to the terrain, and protection from sun and rain.
Below is a core list, followed by extras for each type of trip. Many items, from sleeping bags to ski gear and wetsuits, can be rented locally, so you do not need to buy everything.
quickAnswer: For an adventure trip in India, pack a layering system (base layer, fleece, insulated jacket, waterproof shell), footwear suited to the activity, sun protection, a rain jacket, a headlamp, a first-aid kit, water bottles and your documents. Add microspikes and warm gloves for snow, quick-dry clothes and strapped sandals for rafting and water sports, and a scarf and sunglasses for the desert. Rent bulky gear locally.
takeaways: Layers beat one heavy jacket: base, mid, insulated and waterproof.
Break in trekking shoes before the trip; never start a trek in new boots.
Avoid cotton and denim for water sports and treks; they stay wet and cold.
Sun protection matters everywhere, most of all at altitude and on water.
Sleeping bags, ski gear, wetsuits and trekking poles can usually be rented.

sections.heading: The core list (every trip)
list: Base layers: two quick-dry T-shirts and one thermal top and bottom
Mid layer: a fleece or wool jumper
Insulated layer: a down or synthetic jacket (for hills and nights)
Waterproof jacket and, for the monsoon or snow, waterproof trousers
Trekking trousers (not jeans) and a pair of shorts
Socks: synthetic or wool, one pair per two days
A cap or sun hat, a warm beanie, and sunglasses with UV protection
Sunscreen (SPF 30 to 50) and lip balm with SPF
A daypack of 20 to 30 litres
Headlamp with spare batteries
Two 1-litre water bottles or a hydration bladder
Power bank and charging cables
A small towel and basic toiletries

rows: Broken-in trekking shoes with ankle support and good grip
Waterproof trekking shoes, gaiters, microspikes (often provided)
Sandals with heel straps or old sports shoes
Closed shoes or sandals; sand gets very hot
Riding boots or sturdy ankle-high shoes

items.name: Himalayan treks
body: A 40 to 60 litre backpack with rain cover, sleeping bag rated for the lowest night temperature (often rentable), trekking poles, gloves (inner and outer), a buff or neck warmer, water purification tablets and energy snacks.

items.name: Snow treks and skiing
body: Down jacket, two sets of thermals, waterproof gloves, woollen socks, goggles or UV sunglasses, gaiters and microspikes; ski clothing and equipment can be rented at Gulmarg, Auli and Solang.

items.name: Rafting, kayaking and water sports
body: Quick-dry shorts and T-shirt, a rash guard, sandals with straps, a dry bag or waterproof phone pouch, sunglasses with a strap, waterproof sunscreen and a full change of clothes.

items.name: Diving and snorkelling
body: Swimwear, rash guard, reef-safe sunscreen, your own mask if you have one, certification card and logbook, and motion-sickness tablets for boats.

items.name: Desert trips
body: A wide hat, a scarf for sand and sun, sunglasses, light long sleeves for the day and warm layers for winter nights, a torch and lip balm.

items.name: High-altitude road trips (Ladakh, Spiti)
body: Riding gear if on a motorcycle, thermals and a down jacket, a rain suit, spare fuel container, tool kit and spares, cash and offline maps.

sections.heading: First-aid kit and health
list: Personal prescription medicines, with a copy of the prescription
Paracetamol and an anti-inflammatory for pain
Oral rehydration salts
Anti-diarrhoea tablets and antacids
Antiseptic cream, plasters, blister pads and crepe bandage
Motion-sickness tablets for winding roads and boats
Insect repellent
Altitude medication only on a doctor's advice

sections.heading: Documents
list: Government photo ID (and passport for foreign nationals)
Printed permits (Inner Line, Protected Area, national park)
Driving licence, vehicle papers and insurance for road trips
Travel and activity insurance details
Diving certification card if certified
Emergency contacts on paper, not only on your phone

sections.heading: What to rent instead of buy

rows: Trek operators and rental shops in Manali, Rishikesh, Dehradun, Leh
Rental shops in trekking hubs and Leh

safety: Pack for the coldest and wettest conditions you might meet, not the average.
Keep layers and rain gear in your daypack, not in the main bag on a mule or jeep.
Carry enough personal medicines for the whole trip plus spares.
Keep documents in a waterproof pouch.

faqs.q: What should I pack for a trek in India?
faqs.a: Layers (base, fleece, insulated jacket, waterproof shell), broken-in trekking shoes, a backpack with rain cover, headlamp, water bottles, sun protection and a first-aid kit.

faqs.q: What should I wear for river rafting?
faqs.a: Quick-dry shorts and a synthetic T-shirt, sandals with heel straps or old sports shoes, and sunglasses with a strap. Avoid cotton and jeans.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Ladakh?
faqs.a: Thermals, a down jacket, UV sunglasses, high-SPF sunscreen, lip balm, a water bottle and a basic medical kit, plus riding gear for motorcycle trips.

faqs.q: Can I rent trekking gear in India?
faqs.a: Yes. Sleeping bags, tents, jackets and poles are rented in hubs such as Manali, Rishikesh, Dehradun and Leh, and by trek operators.

faqs.q: What should I pack for a desert safari?
faqs.a: A hat, scarf, sunglasses, sunscreen, light long sleeves for the day and warm layers for winter nights.
